analysis.title: US Equity Positioning Update: Better Earnings Could Trigger Short Squeeze In AI Names
key_insights: US hedge funds continued to de-risk last week, with the pressure concentrated in AI. Selling shifted from Semis toward Hyperscalers, with the strongest two-day reduction in Hyperscaler longs since covid, before funds reversed course on Friday.

The broader positioning trend is toward lower AI beta, with long exposure cut while AI shorts increase. The reduction in longs and the surge in shorts pushed Nets to the 17th percentile on a 1-year lookback, which UBS says exposes the potential for a short squeeze on better-than-expected earnings.
Composite manager positioning flipped to 0.5 standard deviations underweight from overweight the prior week. UBS notes this adds another potential buyer on a move higher.
Systematic investors are split. CTAs have been persistent equity sellers for weeks and cut exposure to the 11th percentile last week. Risk Control exposure remains near highs at the 93rd percentile.
A 2% decline in SPX is estimated to trigger $155bn of Risk Control selling. High Risk Control exposure limits scope to add risk.

Into month-end, Pension and Target Date funds are estimated to buy about $30bn of equities, but only $3.7bn of that demand will be in US equities. Pension buying is not a US story. Target date funds are still seeing inflows.
Corporates are still in the buyback quiet period around earnings.
This week is the busiest earnings week of the quarter and UBS expects it to determine the short-term direction of equities.

The average option-implied earnings move this season is 5.4%, below last quarter but in line with longer-term averages. Tech names imply an average move of 7.3%, the smallest in the past four quarters, which UBS describes as cheap.
Early reporters are underperforming their implied moves by the widest margin since covid.
